title: Within-SNR frame parallelism for SimulationRunner
description:
## Goal

Add within-SNR frame parallelism to `SimulationRunner` so a single
SNR point can saturate all available cores. Today `run_with_decoder`
(`crates/gf2-coding/src/simulation.rs:3828`) and `run_coded_iterative`
process frames serially within an SNR point; the only existing
parallel variant, `run_coded_iterative_parallel`, parallelises
**across** SNR points only. The DVB-T2 production campaign
(`e4849f07`) cannot reach the FER=10⁻⁴ frame-error target in
reasonable wall-clock without this.

## Why now

Measured during the 2026-06-05 production launch of `e4849f07`:
single-thread throughput is **1.6 frames/sec** on AMD Ryzen 9 5900X
for the DVB-T2 r1/2 16-QAM SumProduct chain (n_ldpc=64800,
bits/sym=4, ExactLogMap demap). At the [hard] criterion of ≥100
errors at the FER≈10⁻⁴ bracket point, this is ~10⁶ frames ≈ **7
days per deep SNR point per config × 6 configs**. The runner uses
`NLWP=2` (one worker + main thread) at 100% on a single core out of
24 — `verified via ps -o pid,nlwp,pcpu` during the run.

Partial r1/2 16-QAM data already collected (preserved in
`dev/benchmarks/dvb_t2_awgn/curve_1_2_16qam/checkpoints/`) shows the
implementation is on-target: FER=0.465 at Es/N0=6.0 dB (ETSI
threshold), FER<2.7e-5 at Es/N0=6.25 dB after 37 555 frames. The
≤0.5 dB gap target is plausibly met; we just cannot formally
bracket it in current wall-clock budget.

## Deliverables

1. New parallel API on `SimulationRunner` that dispatches frames
   within one SNR point across rayon workers. Either a new method
   (e.g. `run_with_decoder_parallel`) or a `parallelism: usize`
   parameter on `run_with_decoder`. Caller surface to be decided
   during design — the campaign binary
   (`crates/gf2-coding/src/bin/dvb_t2_awgn_campaign.rs:971`) must
   be able to opt in without losing observability features (tracing,
   checkpointing).
2. Determinism: result CSV columns (`fer`, `frames`, `errors`,
   `mean_iters`) must be **byte-identical** to a single-thread run
   at the same seed. Each worker owns an independent
   `ChaCha20Rng::set_word_pos`-ed clone, advancing by a fixed
   chunk-size step; aggregation is order-independent (sum of
   per-worker counts).
3. Heartbeat / checkpoint behaviour: at minimum, per-SNR-boundary
   checkpoint as in `run_coded_iterative_parallel`. Within-SNR
   heartbeat resume is a nice-to-have; if architecturally hard, can
   defer with a follow-up issue.
4. Update campaign binary to use the new parallel API by default,
   with a CLI knob to opt back to single-thread for byte-identity
   regression tests.

## Success criteria

- [hard] Property test: parallel run on N workers (N ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8})
  produces byte-identical `fer`, `frames`, `errors`, `mean_iters`
  vs single-thread for the same seed across at least 3 (rate, mod)
  configurations (e.g. r1/2 16qam, r2/3 64qam, r3/4 64qam).
- [hard] Throughput on AMD Ryzen 9 5900X (24 threads) ≥ **12x**
  single-thread for DVB-T2 r1/2 16-QAM at Es/N0=6.5 dB (deep
  waterfall, low mean_iters case). Reported in
  `dev/benchmarks/dvb_t2_awgn/parallel_throughput.md`.
- [hard] Campaign binary integrates the new API; running r1/2
  16-QAM at the existing 0.25 dB bracket completes with ≥100
  errors at every bracket point in ≤ 24h wall-clock.
- [hard] No new `unsafe`; satisfies `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`
  outside the kernel crates.
- [hard] Documentation: `crates/gf2-coding/src/simulation.rs`
  module-level rustdoc updated; CLAUDE.md "Test tiers" /
  "Architecture" sections updated where the runner is described.

## Non-goals

- No new channel models.
- No changes to the encoder, decoder, or BICM chain.
- GPU dispatch path remains the existing `--gpu` reservation.

## Notes for the implementer

- `ChaCha20Rng::set_word_pos` is already used by the
  resume/checkpoint path (`simulation.rs`); the per-worker offset
  scheme is a natural extension.
- The current per-frame cost (~0.6 s for r1/2 16-QAM) is
  encoder+demap+decode-dominated; ensure the IRA encoder cache
  (`crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/encoding/`) and decoder state are
  safely shareable across workers (immutable codec, mutable
  per-worker scratch).
- Coordinate with the existing tracing/Subscriber install in
  `run_coded_iterative_parallel` (see comment around line 3486 for
  per-rayon-worker `Dispatch` propagation).
